s: Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord
3500.full: αὐτόματος -ον, and -η, -ον (etym. doubtful; see Boisacq, Prellwitz, see word), [in LXX, Lev.25:5, 11, 4Ki.19:29 (סָפִיחַ), Jos.6:5, Job.24:24, Wis.17:6 * ;] __1. of persons, acting of one's own will. __2. Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord: γῆ Mrk.4:28 (MM, see word); πύλη, Act.12:10.† (AS)

3501.full: 1. the neck, throat , of men and beasts, (Homer), etc. 2. metaphorically any narrow passage, a neck of land, isthmus , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a narrow sea, strait , (Herdotus Historicus); of the point at which the Danube spreads into several branches, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a narrow mountain-pass, defile , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound
3502.full: 1. a furrow made in ploughing, Lat. sulcus, (Homer), etc.; αὔλακ᾽ ἐλαύνειν to draw a furrow , (Hesiod) 2. metaphorically of a wife as the bearer of children , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically also, a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. = ὄγμος, a swathe , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (Prob. from same Root as ὁλκός, Lat. sulcus, from ἕλκω.) (ML)

3504.lxx: in LXX: β. φέρειν, Gen.31:35 (חרה בעיני); β. ἀκούειν, Isa.6:10 (כּבד hi.)*
3504.full: βαρέως, adv. (βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, Gen.31:35 (חרה בעיני); β. ἀκούειν, Isa.6:10 (כּבד hi.)* ;] heavily, with difficulty: Mat.13:15, Act.28:27" (LXX) .† (AS)

3505.lxx: in LXX: Jdg.16:30 (נטה), Rut.2:16, 2Ki.23:5, 4Ki.18:14 and Job.21:3 (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 *
3505.full: βαστάζω, [in LXX: Jdg.16:30 (נטה), Rut.2:16, 2Ki.23:5, 4Ki.18:14 and Job.21:3 (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 * ;] __1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jhn.10:31. __2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaphorically, to endure; Mat.3:11 20:12, Mrk.14:13, Luk.7:14 10:7 11:27 14:27 22:10, Jhn.16:12 19:17, Act.3:2 9:15 15:1 21:35, Rom.11:18 15:1, Gal.5:10 6:2, 5 17, Rev.2:2, 3 17:7. __3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x), __(a) to take away; Mat.8:17 (Isa.53:4, Heb.); __(b) to carry off, steal: Jhn.12:6 20:15. † (AS)

3507.full: βιόω, -ῶ (βίος), [in LXX: Pro.7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job.29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;] to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).† SYN.: ζάω (which see). (AS)

3508.full: βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ (βλάσφημος), [in LXX: Eze.35:12 (נֶאָצָה), Da TH 3:29 (96) (שׁלה), Tob.1:18, 1Ma.2:6, 2Ma.8:4 10:35 15:24 * ;] __(a) railing slander: Mat.12:31 15:19, Mrk.3:28 7:22, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.6:4, Ju 9, Rev.2:9 __(b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: Mat.26:65, Mrk.14:64, Luk.5:21, Jhn.10:33, Rev.13:5; ὄνομα βλασφημίας, Rev.13:1 17:3; with genitive obj. Mat.12:31; πρὸς τ. θεόν, Rev.13:6 (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).† (AS)

3509.full: βλάσφημος, -ον (βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Isa.66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 10:4, 36 * ;] __(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Act.6:11, 2Ti.3:2, 2Pe.2:11 (cf. Ju 9); __(b) as subst. a blasphemer: 1Ti.1:13 (Cremer, 570). † (AS)

3510.full: βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Exo.15:5, Neh.9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Psa.67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;] __1. the bottom. __2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2Co.11:25. † (AS)

3511.full: 1. an acorn , Lat. glans, the fruit of the φηγός, given to swine, (Odyssey by Homer):—; any similar fruit, the date , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. from similarity of shape, an iron peg, a bolt-pin , Lat. pessulus, passed through the wooden bar ( μοχλός) into the door-post, so that the bar could not be removed till the pin was taken out with a hook ( βαλανάγρα), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

3512.full: a flat-bottomed boat , used in Egypt, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

3516.lxx: in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc.
3516.full: δειλία, -ας, ἡ (δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;] cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): 2Ti.1:7.† SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).† (AS)

3518.lxx: in LXX for ספר pi., etc.
3518.full: δι-αγγέλω [in LXX for ספר pi., etc. ;] to publish abroad, proclaim: with accusative, Luk.9:60, Act.21:26, Rom.9:17" (LXX) .† (AS)

3520.full: 1. to send off in different directions, send to and fro, send about or round , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to send over or across , (Aristophanes Comicus): to transmit , ἐπιστολήν (Thucydides); so in Mid., (Thucydides) (ML)

s: to rub hard, rub away, consume
3521.full: δια-τρίβω [in LXX Lev.14:8 (יָשַׁב), Jer.35:7 (גּוּר), Tob.11:8, 12, Jdth.10:2, 2Ma.14:23 * ;] to rub hard, rub away, consume; δ. χρόνον, ἡμέρας, to spend time: Act.14:3, 28 16:12 20:6 25:6, 14. Intransitively with ellipse of object (El., § 81, 1), to spend time, stay: Jhn.3:22 11:54, Act.15:35, Act.12:19.† (AS)

3525.full: 1. a crossing over, passage , δ. ποιεῖσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a means or place of crossing , (Herdotus Historicus): δ. ποταμοῦ a ford , (Thucydides): a bridge , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

3527.full: διό-περ conjunct. (διό, which see, strengthened by πέρ), [in LXX: Jdth.8:17; Jdt.8.1-36; 2Ma.5:1-27 * ;] for which very reason: 1Co.8:13 10:14.† (AS)

3528.full: δοκός, -οῦ, ἡ (δέχομαι) [in LXX for קוֹרָה, etc. ;] a beam of timber: Mat.7:3-5, Luk.6:41-42 (DCG, i, 176).† (AS)

3530.full: δουλόω, -ῶ (δοῦλος), [in LXX for עָבַד ;] to enslave, bring into bondage: Act.7:6 (LXX), 2Pe.2:19; metaphorically, 1Co.9:19; pass., before ἐν, 1Co.7:15; τ. θεῷ, Rom.6:22; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Rom.6:18; οἴνῳ, Tit.2:3; ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, Gal.4:3 (Cremer, 217).† (AS)

3532.lxx: in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), Psa.12:6; and as seel. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זָקַק pual.), 1Ch.29:4 (Bab); εἰ δ .ίστιν (יְקָר), Zec.11:13 א with a vid, Q *)*
3532.full: δοκίμιος, -α, -ον (δοκιμή), [in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), Psa.12:6; and as seel. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זָקַק pual.), 1Ch.29:4 (Bab); εἰ δ .ίστιν (יְקָר), Zec.11:13 א with a vid, Q *)* ;] = δόκιμος, tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, 1Pe.1:7 (where Hort suggests the seel. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), Jas.1:3 (but see Mayor, in l For full discussion of this word, not hitherto found in a Gk. Lexicon, and for exx. of its use in π., see Deiss. (to whom is due the credit of its discovery), BS, 259 ff.; MM, Exp., xi; cf. also Milligan, NTD, 76).† δόκιμος, -ον (δέκομαι = δέχομαι) [in LXX for זָקַק pual., etc. ;] primarily of metals, tested, accepted, approved: of persons, Rom.14:18 16:10, 1Co.11:19, 2Co.10:18 13:7, 2Ti.2:15, Jas.1:12 (Cremer, 212, 697).† (AS)

3534.full: εὐεργεσία, -ας, ἡ (εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Psa.78:11 (עֲלִילָה), Wis.16:11, 24, 2Ma.6:13 2Mac 9:26, 4Ma.8:17 * ;] a good deed, kindness, benefit: 1Ti.6:2; with genitive of person(s) (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), Act.4:9,† (AS)

3535.full: ζημόω, -ῶ (ζημία), [in LXX chiefly for עָנַשׁ ;] to damage. Pass., to suffer loss, forfeit, lose: absol., 1Co.3:15; before ἐν, 2Co.7:9; with accusative of thing(s) (see B1., § 34, 6), τ. ψυχήν, Mat.16:26, Mrk.8:36; ἑαυτόν, Luk.9:25; τ. πάντα, Php.3:8.† (AS)

s: In LXX and NT, to make alive, cause to live, quicken
3536.lxx: in LXX for חָיָה pi., hi., Jdg.21:14, 4Ki.5:7, Neh.9:6, Job.36:6, Psa.70:20, Ecc.7:12 *
3536.full: ζωο-ποιέω, ῶ [in LXX for חָיָה pi., hi., Jdg.21:14, 4Ki.5:7, Neh.9:6, Job.36:6, Psa.70:20, Ecc.7:12 * ;] __1. in cl. (= ζωογονέω), to produce alive. __2. In LXX and NT, to make alive, cause to live, quicken (DCG, ii, 606a; Cremer, 275): Jhn.5:21 6:53, Rom.4:17 8:11, 1Co.15:45, 2Co.3:6, Gal.3:21. Pass., 1Co.15:22 15:36, 1Pe.3:18.† (AS)

3537.full: ζήτησις, -εως, ἡ (ζητέω). __1. a seeking, search. __2. a questioning, inquiry, debate: Act.15:2, 7, 2Ti.2:23, Tit.3:9; before περί, Jhn.3:26, Act.25:20, 1Ti.6:4.† (AS)

3538.full: θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (θεοσεβής), [in LXX Gen.20:11 (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאָה), Job.28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Sir.1:24, Bar.5:4, 4Ma.7:6 4Mac 7:22, א 4Ma.15:28 א 4Ma.17:15 * ;] fear of God, godliness: 1Ti.2:10.† (AS)

3539.lxx: in LXX for עֶבֶד Gen.45:16 (cf. Est.5:2), etc.
3539.full: θεραπεία, -ας, ἡ (θεραπεύω) [in LXX for עֶבֶד Gen.45:16 (cf. Est.5:2), etc. ;] __1. service. __2. healing: Luk.9:11 (Field, Notes, 60), Rev.22:2. __3. Collective, household attendants, servants: Luk.12:42 (LXX, ll. with).† (AS)

3542.full: 1. to bloom, abound, to be luxuriant , of fruit-trees, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; often in participle perfect τεθηλώς, epic feminine τεθαλυῖα, as adjective, luxuriant, exuberant , (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate, οὐ δένδρε᾽ ἔθαλλεν χῶρος the place grew no trees, θαλλούσης βίον ἐλαίας (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of other natural objects, τεθαλυῖα ἐέρση the fresh or copious dew, (Odyssey by Homer); τεθαλυῖα ἀλοιφῆι rich with fat, (Iliad by Homer); εἰλαπίνηι τεθαλυίηι at a sumptuous feast, (Iliad by Homer) 3. of men, to bloom, flourish , (Hesiod), etc. 4. in bad sense, to be active , νόσος ἀεὶ τέθηλε (Sophocles Tragicus); πήματα ἀεὶ θάλλοντα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

3545.full: καθ-οπλίζω [in LXX: Jer.46:9 (תָּפַשׂ), Mac.9* ;] to arm fully: pass., Luk.11:21.† (AS)

3546.full: to make new : hence, καί τι καινίζει στέγη and the house has something strange about it, (Sophocles Tragicus); καίνισον ζυγόν try on thy new yoke, handsel it, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. εὐχάς to offer new, strange prayers, (Euripides) (ML)

s: to speak ill of, revile, abuse
3547.full: κακολογέω, -ῶ (κακολόγος, slanderous), [in LXX: Exo.21:16 22:28, 1Ki.3:13, Pro.20:20, Eze.22:7 (קָלַל pi., hi.), 2Ma.4:1 * ;] to speak ill of, revile, abuse: with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:4, Mrk.7:10" (LXX) Mrk.9:39; with accusative of thing(s), Act.19:9.† (AS)

3548.full: κακοήθεια (WH, -θία), -ας, ἡ (κακός, ἦθος), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 3Ma.3:22 3Mac 7:3 A, 4Ma.1:4 4Mac 3:4 * ;] malignity, malevolence: Rom.1:29 (Cremer, 329).† (AS)

3550.full: 1. strong, staunch, stout, sturdy; with infinitive, καρτερὸς ἐναίρειν strong to kill, (Iliad by Homer); τὰ καρτερώτατα the strongest , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with genitive possessed of a thing, lord or master of it, (Theognis Elegiacus) 3. like καρτερικός, steadfast, patient , πρὸς πάντα (Xenophon Historicus): obstinate , (Plato Philosophus) 4. of things, strong, mighty, potent , ὅρκος (Iliad by Homer); κ. ἔργα deeds of might , (Iliad by Homer); κ. μάχη strongly contested, desperate , (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ καρτερόν, τόλμης τὸ κ. the extremity of daring, (Euripides):—; κατὰ τὸ καρτερόν by force , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, πρὸς τὸ καρτερόν (Aeschulus Tragicus); τὸ καρτερόν, absolute, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 5. of place, like ὀχυρός, strong , (Thucydides); τὸ καρτερώτερον τοῦ χωρίου (Thucydides) 6. adverb -ρῶς, strongly , etc., κ. ὑπνοῦσθαι to sleep soundly , (Herdotus Historicus) 7. the common comparative and Sup. are κρείσσων and κράτιστος (qq. see.): but the regular forms καρτερώτερος, -ώτατος, occur now and then, (Pindar), attic (ML)

3552.full: to cry down, cry out against , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus); κ. τινῶν ὅτι τὰς σπονδὰς λελυκότες εἶεν (Thucydides); with accusative to bawl down, outcry , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

3554.full: to portion out :—;Mid. to receive as one's portion , (Plutarch) (ML)

3558.full: 1. to besprinkle or bespatter , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., καταπαττόμενος (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. with accusative rei, to sprinkle or strew over , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: to strike down with an arrow, shoot dead
3560.full: κατα-τοξεύω [in LXX: Exo.19:13 (יָרָה), al. ;] to strike down with an arrow, shoot dead: Heb.12:20 (LXX) (Rec.; WH, R, om.).† (AS)

3562.full: κατενώπιον adv. (= Hom., κατένωπα), [in LXX: Psa.44:15, al. ;] over against, before: with genitive, τ. δόξης, Ju 24; metaphorically (cf. κατέναντι, and see Lft., Col., l.with), τ. θεοῦ, Eph.1:4, Col.1:22.† (AS)

3563.lxx: in LXX for יָקֹשׁ ni., etc.
3563.full: κινδυνεύω (κίνδυνος), [in LXX for יָקֹשׁ ni., etc. ;] __1. to be daring, to venture. __2. to be in danger: Luk.8:23, Act.19:27, 40, 1Co.15:30.† (AS)

3564.full: κλοπή, -ῆν, ἡ (κλέπτω), [in LXX for גָּנַב ;] theft: pl., Mat.15:19, Mrk.7:22.† (AS)

3565.full: the part between the knee and ankle, the leg , Lat. tibia, (Homer), etc. (ML)

3566.lxx: in LXX: Pro.28:24, Isa.1:23 (חָבֵר), Mal.2:14 (חֲבֶרֶת), Est.8:13, al.
3566.full: κοινωνός, -ή, -όν (κοινός), [in LXX: Pro.28:24, Isa.1:23 (חָבֵר), Mal.2:14 (חֲבֶרֶת), Est.8:13, al. ;] __1. as adj., = κοινός. __2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ κ., __(a) a partner, associate, companion: 2Co.8:23, Phm 17; with dative of person(s), Luk.5:10; with genitive of person(s), Heb.10:33; id. before ἐν, Mat.23:30; __(b) a partaker, sharer: with genitive of thing(s), 1Co.10:18 10:20, 2Co.1:7, 1Pe.5:1, 2Pe.1:4 (see Deiss., BS, 368 n2).† (AS)

3568.full: 1. a half-boot , (Xenophon Historicus):—; κρηπῖδες soldiers' boots , i. e. soldiers themselves, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. generally, a groundwork, foundation, basement of a temple or altar, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, κρηπὶς σοφῶν ἐπέων (Pindar); οὐδέπω κρηπὶς κακῶν ὕπεστι we have not yet got to the bottom of misery, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ ἐγκράτεια ἀρετῆς κρηπίς self-control is the foundation of virtue, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the walled edge of a river, a quay , Lat. crepido, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

3569.lxx: in LXX: 3Ki.7:7 (מִשְׁפָּט), Dan LXX TH Dan.7:10, 26, (דִּין), Su 1:49, Exo.21:6, Jdg.5:10 *
3569.full: κριτήριον, -ου, τό (κριτής), [in LXX: 3Ki.7:7 (מִשְׁפָּט), Dan LXX TH Dan.7:10, 26, (דִּין), Su 1:49, Exo.21:6, Jdg.5:10 * ;] __1. a means of judging, test, criterion. __2. a tribunal: 1Co.6:2 6:4, Jas.2:6.† (AS)

3571.full: κτίσμα, -τος, τό (κτίζω), [in LXX: Wis.9:2 13:5 14:11, Sir.36:20 (17), Sir.38:34, 3Ma.5:11 * ;] __1. (cl.) a colony. __2. a created thing, creature: 1Ti.4:4, Jas.1:18, Rev.5:13 8:9.† (AS)

3575.full: κάμνω [in LXX: Job.10:1 (קוּט ni.) Job.17:2, Wis.4:16 15:9, 4Ma.3:8 4Mac 7:13 * ;] __1. to work; hence, from the effect of continued work, __2. to be weary: Heb.12:3 __3. to be sick: Jas.5:15.† (AS)

3577.full: the tail of a beast, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

3578.full: a bell , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in fortified towns an officer went round at night with a bell to challenge the sentries, and see that they were awake, (Thucydides); ὡς κώδωνα ἐξαψάμενος like one with an alarm-bell in his hand, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

3580.full: λαμπρός, -ά, -όν (λάμπω), [in LXX: Tob.13:11, Wis.6:12 17:20, Sir.29:22 33:13 (Sir.30:25) Sir.31:23, Ep. Je 60 * ;] bright, brilliant: ποταμός, Rev.22:1 (ΕΥ, clear); ἀστήρ, Rev.22:16; of clothing, brilliant, splendid: Luk.23:11, Act.10:30, Jas.2:2-3, Rev.15:6 18:14 19:8.† (AS)

3581.full: λαμπρότης, -ητος, ἡ [in LXX: Psa.110:3 (הָדָר), al. ;] brightness, brilliancy: τ. ἡλίου, Act.26:13.† (AS)

3583.full: λατομέω, -ῶ (λατόμος, a stonecutter, 4Ki.12:12, al.; λᾶς, τέμνω; cf. λαξευτός) [in LXX: 1Ch.22:2, al. (חָצַב); Exo.21:33, Num_21:18 (כָּרָה) ;] to hew, hew out stones: Mat.27:60, Mrk.15:46.† (AS)

3584.lxx: in LXX for עֲבֹדָה, שָׁרַת; ἔργα, Num_7:5; στολαί Exo.31:10 39:32; σκευή, Num.4:12, 26, 2Ch.24:14 *
3584.full: λειτουργικός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for עֲבֹדָה, שָׁרַת; ἔργα, Num_7:5; στολαί Exo.31:10 39:32; σκευή, Num.4:12, 26, 2Ch.24:14 * ;] of or for service, ministering: πνεύματα, Heb.1:14.† (AS)

3586.full: λεπίς, -ίδος, ἡ (λέπω, to peel) [in LXX chiefly for קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת ;] a scale: Act.9:18† (AS)

s: to be gone, to be wanting
3587.full: λείπω [in LXX: Job.4:11, Pro.19:4 (פָּרַד), al. ;] __1. trans., to leave, leave behind; pass., to be left behind, to lack before prep. (as more usual in cl.), ἐν, Jas.1:4; with genitive of thing(s), Jas.1:5 2:15. __2. Intrans., to be gone, to be wanting: with dative of person(s), Luk.18:22, Tit.3:13; τὰ λείποντα, Tit.1:5 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, ἐν-κατα-, περι-, ὑπο-λείπω).† (AS)

s: painfully, so as to cause pain
3588.full: 1. of things, painful, distressing , Lat. molestus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. of persons, 3. in good sense, causing sorrow by one's departure, (Euripides) 4. in bad sense, causing pain, troublesome, vexatious, offensive , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 5. adverb λυπηρῶς, painfully, so as to cause pain , (Sophocles Tragicus); λυπηρῶς ἔχει it is painful , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

3591.lxx: in LXX: Hos.9:7-8 מַשְׂטֵמָה), Wis.5:4, al.
3591.full: μανία, -ας, ἡ (μαίνομαι) [in LXX: Hos.9:7-8 מַשְׂטֵמָה), Wis.5:4, al. ;] frenzy, madness: Act.26:24.† (AS)
